decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm approach to mouse, lifting and pitching gradually while keeping left arm parked and configuration continuous.
Move above mouse and continue wrist pitch toward a top grasp; use RGB to refine before descending.
Refine mouse alignment: advance while finishing downward pitch and lower slowly with gripper open.
Small final mouse alignment, close fully, and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Carry the visibly lifted mouse rightward toward the pad, maintaining closed grasp and modest table clearance.
Previous carry was rejected before motion. Use much smaller lateral increments and slightly relax wrist pitch to preserve IK continuity while retaining mouse.
Further reduce the initial retraction to submillimeter increments following zero-step IK rejection; keep mouse closed and avoid an elbow branch change.
Short lateral carry test; mouse retention is uncertain from its changing wrist-image position, so inspect before proceeding farther.
Mouse did not follow the lateral test. Reopen and realign above its new position with a lower, farther-forward approach.
Center the mouse more precisely between open fingers, descend slightly, then close fully for a second grasp attempt.
Replan after IK interruption: retract wrist slightly and reduce downward pitch so fingers can reach forward without driving the elbow toward its limit.
Retry the wrist-unpitch maneuver at smaller initial increments after zero executed steps; maintain an open gripper and continuous elbow configuration.
Mouse is now centered in the wrist view. Close at the refined pose and perform a small lift/retraction to check retention.
Carry the apparently retained mouse toward the pad with a small clearance lift; maintain closed gripper and inspect its motion.
Mouse follows the gripper. Translate over the pad center while maintaining clearance and a fully closed target.
Lower and release mouse on the pad, then lift clear. Begin an elevated left-arm approach toward the keyboard without crossing workspaces.
Withdraw the right hand from the released mouse and stage both hands on their respective sides of the keyboard for a controlled push.
Align closed grippers near the keyboard's front corners; right arm descends from clearance while left makes a small contact approach.
Make a small coordinated forward push from both keyboard corners and inspect whether contact is moving the board evenly.
The board did not move; fingers were above its edge. Retract both hands and lower modestly to establish a front-edge push rather than passing over the keys.
Contact is visible at the keyboard front edge. Push slowly forward and slightly right, using current tracked heights to avoid forcing into the table.
Keyboard now moves with the front-edge contact. Continue a balanced diagonal push toward the outlined frame while keeping each hand on its own side.
Finish the small forward-right alignment of the keyboard with the frame, maintaining matched contact on both corners.
Release the aligned keyboard and withdraw both hands upward and back. Prepare the left arm for the figurine while keeping the right clear of the mouse.
Approach the figurine from its left workspace with the left hand open, while returning the right arm toward its initial pose.
Refine the left-hand alignment toward the figurine's torso using the wrist image; keep fingers open and move slowly clear of the clock.
Make a small final torso adjustment, close the left gripper fully, and test figurine retention with a short vertical lift.
Lift the gripped figurine clear of the table and clock before moving toward the small stand; verify the base follows.
Figurine did not remain held. Reopen and approach lower around its torso instead of the sloping shoulder, correcting leftward and forward alignment.
Shift left to center the figurine's narrower torso, close fully, and perform another cautious lift test.
Lift and make a short lateral retention test of the figurine before committing to the transfer; keep the gripper closed.
Figurine follows the lifted gripper. Carry it above the clock toward the stand, retaining height and staying in the left workspace.
Figurine shifted in the grasp and brushed the clock. Increase clearance slowly before further placement, keeping the left gripper closed.
Figurine has slipped and is lying on the table. Reopen and approach its torso from above rather than repeating the unstable shoulder grasp.
Descend toward the fallen figurine's torso with open fingers, adjusting away from the drawer front and clock.
Descent was obstructed near the drawer. Back away slightly and rotate toward a vertical grasp before attempting to descend again.
With the wrist clear of the drawer, align over the fallen figurine's waist and descend gradually, leaving the gripper open.
Figurine was displaced toward the drawer. Move clear and align with the accessible alarm clock first, avoiding further contact with the drawer obstruction.
Center the alarm clock between the open fingers with a small rightward/backward adjustment and close around its sides.
Lift the centered alarm clock vertically, keeping the gripper closed, and verify that it follows before carrying it over the drawer.
The clock remains between the fingers. Raise its bottom above the drawer rim while translating left toward the tray, preserving the current grasp.
Replan after five executed steps: stop raising, move left with a gentle wrist unpitch to avoid the folding limit while keeping the clock in front of the drawer.
Raise the retained clock in small increments while easing forward and unpitching, monitoring clearance from the drawer front and elbow continuity.
After the one-step interruption, hold EE height and unpitch the wrist gradually with slight retraction to gain clock clearance without increasing the elbow bend.
Clock slipped during wrist rotation. Reopen and approach its new position using the shallower wrist angle, so the next lift can keep orientation fixed.
Align with the face-up clock and descend around its side walls, then close without changing wrist orientation.
The fingers closed above the clock face. Reopen, gain a little clearance, and align the closing direction with the clock's flat sides before a deeper grasp.
Lower the aligned open fingers to the clock's side-wall height, with a slight backward correction; inspect before closing to avoid another shallow grasp.
Close at the deeper side-wall alignment and lift only three centimeters to verify the clock follows before committing to the drawer transfer.
Clock did not lift. Reopen and level the fingers into a vertical approach aligned with the clock sides, compensating forward for the wrist pitch change.
Descend the now-level fingers around the clock's sides with a small forward correction, then close fully at the lower grasp height.
The closing motion pushed the clock rather than capturing it. Open, lift slightly, and shift toward its displaced center before another closure.
Lift clear before a small forward-right correction, then descend vertically and close to avoid sweeping the clock away during alignment.
Test this deeper clock grasp with a slow upward-left motion while keeping the wrist fixed and the gripper closed.
The clock did not follow: the pinch was left of its center. Reopen and shift above the visible clock center, keeping the vertical, side-aligned approach.
Open fingers are contacting the clock diagonally. Lift clear and adjust yaw to align the jaws with its flat sides rather than forcing a wider diagonal grasp.
Correct the yaw direction from the new wrist view and make a small centering adjustment while staying above the clock.
Replan from the actual pose after substantial tracking error. Stop yawing and make a small, slow correction toward the clock center and side-wall height.
Large tracking error indicates obstruction. Withdraw and lift before further lateral alignment rather than pressing down against the clock or drawer.
Reapproach with a backward-left correction accounting for the offset from link6 to the fingertips; descend slowly with fingers open.
The wrist view shows the clock still ahead of the fingers. Advance the open hand at fixed height to center it before any further descent.
Tracking shows the wrist obstructed near the drawer. Retreat toward the robot and rightward within the left workspace, easing the wrist angle before a lower side approach.
Use a shallower approach so the fingertips reach the clock while the wrist stays in front of the drawer. Shift left and lower gradually with the gripper open.
Clock is now centered within the open fingers. Lower slightly to side-wall depth, close fully, and test a short lift without changing orientation.
The clock slid left during closure. Reopen and recenter while leveling the two fingers about the approach axis so both contact at the same height.
The clock is centered between level fingers. Descend to its side walls in small increments, then close and pause before testing retention.
One jaw is on the clock face rather than outside it. Open, lift clear, shift left to the displaced center, then descend and close again.
Clock is centered between both fingers. Test retention with a slow lift and slight retraction, keeping wrist orientation fixed and gripper closed.
Clock slipped from the shallow contact. Reopen, recenter leftward, and descend toward the lower body rather than the rounded face, checking clearance before closure.
Stop descending at the tracked contact height. Close around the centered lower body, then make a small vertical retention test without changing wrist angle.
The clock is again left of the closed fingers. Reopen, shift left, and reach farther around its center while maintaining clearance; inspect before closing.
Wrist view is occluded by the drawer. Withdraw to clear space and flatten the approach; repeated top pinches have not retained the clock, so prepare a side grasp.
In clear space, rotate the open jaws toward a vertical opening for a side grasp of the face-up clock's thickness, lowering gradually while remaining in front of it.
